stem: An agriculture study measures crop yield across 5 regions, each containing multiple farms. region A has 10 observations with mean 66.2 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 9.4). region B has 5 observations with mean 76.3 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 4.7). region C has 15 observations with mean 67.5 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 4.6). region D has 15 observations with mean 53.6 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 5.3). region E has 20 observations with mean 54.1 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 7.5). The between-region standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 6.8 and 17.0 tonnes/hectare. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true crop yield for region B, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-region variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for region B: 75.8 tonnes/hectare (shrunk from raw 76.3). Range [74.9, 76.1] as between-region SD varies from 6.8 to 17.0. Pooled mean: 60.6.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 60.6 tonnes/hectare (weighted average of 5 region means).
Shrinkage factor for region B: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/5). At σ_between=11.3: B = 0.967.
Interval [74.9, 76.1] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (76.3) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (60.6) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
